clue.text: Soundly support Mr Spock, for one, in such revelry?

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing this kind of drunken festivity

indicators.note: soundly tells us the phrase is to be judged by how it is said, not how it is spelt

parts.note: to support is to back, and Mr Spock of Star Trek is an example of an alien, giving 'back an alien'

explanation.surface: A Star Trek fan wonders whether cheering on Mr Spock counts as wild partying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back an alien', said aloud, matches the adjective for drunken revels in honour of Bacchus; 'for one' marks Spock as merely an example of an alien.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacchanalian describes riotous drinking parties like the festivals of Bacchus, god of wine.

clue.text: Schoolchild perhaps, one that's getting on plane

definitions.meaning: a pupil who lives in at a boarding school
a passenger who goes aboard an aircraft

explanation.definitionFit: A boarder is both a resident pupil and someone who boards a vehicle such as an aircraft.

clue.text: Youngster's heartily sick, given this sort of equation!

parts.note: a cub is a youngster, as in a young scout or young animal

indicators.note: heartily asks for the heart of the word sick, its central letters

explanation.surface: An exclamation of disgust at a maths problem that makes a young pupil feel ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartily' takes IC, the middle of SICK; the 's of 'Youngster's' and 'given' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A cubic equation is one whose highest power of the unknown is three.

clue.text: Christmas decoration and wine offered in plant

parts.note: holly is the traditional festive greenery hung at Christmas
hock is a British name for German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: Seasonal greenery and a bottle of wine are handed round at a garden party.
explanation.walkthrough: HOCK is the British term for Rhine white wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The hollyhock is a tall garden flower of the mallow family.

clue.text: Square dancing ladies?

definitions.meaning: a number that is another number multiplied by itself, here three times three
in the carol The Twelve Days of Christmas, the ninth day brings ladies dancing

explanation.walkthrough: The carol's ninth gift is 'nine ladies dancing'; the question mark flags that indirect second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is the square of three and the count of the carol's dancing ladies.

clue.text: Relaxes, given evidence veracity levels are rising?

definitions.meaning: takes a rest, stretched out horizontally

definitions.text: given evidence veracity levels are rising?
definitions.meaning: if truthfulness is going up, untruths are falling, read whimsically as a phrase

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a playful literal reading: more truth means fewer falsehoods.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie down is to recline and rest; read literally the phrase means falsehoods decreasing.

clue.text: Simple plants produced liquor — over a gallon drunk?

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling and jumbled, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: ale is a malt liquor

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a gallon of beer was downed, producing the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' rearranges ALE, A and G; 'produced' and 'over' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Algae are primitive plant-like organisms such as seaweeds and pond scum.

clue.text: Bishop wants a source of quartz for church

parts.note: B is the chess notation for a bishop
silica, silicon dioxide, is what quartz is made of

explanation.surface: A cleric wants a supply of a mineral for building his church.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan shows 'a source of quartz'; the OCR dropped 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a large oblong church, often with special privileges from the Pope.

clue.text: Having travelled, nasty feeling one shouldn't have this time?

definitions.text: Having travelled, nasty feeling one shouldn't have this time?

parts.words: Having travelled, nasty feeling one shouldn't have this time?
parts.note: the tiredness after a long flight across time zones, with a pun on 'this time' as the clock time one's body is out of step with

explanation.definitionFit: Jet lag is the fatigue felt after crossing time zones by air, the body clock lagging local time.

clue.text: Using blue light, it may show healthy disrespect for red

definitions.text: Using blue light, it may show healthy disrespect for red

parts.words: Using blue light, it may show healthy disrespect for red
parts.note: an emergency vehicle with flashing blue lamps may drive through red traffic lights, for the sake of patients' health

explanation.definitionFit: An emergency medical vehicle runs on blue lights and may pass red signals.

clue.text: Eat leaves and bark

definitions.meaning: to feed on growing grass or foliage, as cattle do
as a verb, to scrape the skin off, as with a knee

explanation.definitionFit: To graze is to feed on herbage and also to scrape skin, as in barking one's shin.

clue.text: Two weak elements in this bit of verse, after strong start

definitions.text: Two weak elements in this bit of verse, after strong start

parts.words: Two weak elements in this bit of verse, after strong start
parts.note: describes a metrical foot of one stressed syllable followed by two unstressed ones

explanation.definitionFit: A dactyl is a poetic foot of one long or stressed syllable followed by two short ones.

clue.text: Battle's hot — I shall need sharpened blade at the front

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: at the front places the blade's word before the other pieces

parts.note: the edge is the sharpened part of a blade
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
I'll is the contraction of I shall

explanation.surface: A soldier says the fight is fierce and he will need a keen sword in the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: Edgehill (1642) was the first major battle of the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgehill in Warwickshire was the site of the opening battle of the English Civil War.

clue.text: Strongly fancied to win such poker

definitions.meaning: an overwhelming favourite in a race or contest
a ... poker is a garden plant, and literally a fireside iron heated to glowing

explanation.definitionFit: A red-hot favourite is strongly tipped; the red-hot poker is a tall flowering plant.

clue.text: Passionate words in bed —- Rita and I getting excited

indicators.note: getting excited suggests agitation, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: A racy scene of a couple whispering ardently between the sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting excited' rearranges BED, RITA and I; 'in' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter, impassioned verbal attack.

clue.text: Changing Sun's leader at its head office

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Wapping in East London was where The Sun newspaper was produced, its headquarters at the time

explanation.surface: A newspaper's editor is replaced at its headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics mark The Sun, the British tabloid then based at Wapping, east London; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Swapping means exchanging or changing one thing for another.

clue.text: Issuing shares, talking foolishly about gold

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: to prate is to chatter foolishly
OR is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: A company launches a share offer while its spokesman babbles about bullion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talking foolishly' looks like a description of the issuer, but it is the verb prate; OR is the heraldic gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Prorating is allotting in proportion, as when shares are issued pro rata.

clue.text: Sort of drawing that's given to plenipotentiary

definitions.meaning: a sketch made without ruler or tracing
an envoy with full powers is given complete discretion, unrestricted authority

explanation.definitionFit: Freehand drawing is done by eye, and a free hand is full authority to act.

clue.text: Nuts? They'll deal with them

definitions.meaning: nutcrackers, implements for breaking shells of the nuts just mentioned

explanation.definitionFit: Crackers is slang for crazy, and crackers are tools for opening nuts.

clue.text: Napoleon, the first one with no time to ask for help

indicators.note: with no tells us a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: to consult is to seek advice or help

explanation.surface: A historical note about Napoleon being first to manage without help when time ran short.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon was First Consul of France from 1799 to 1804.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte held the title of First Consul before becoming emperor.

clue.text: A junior officer on horse is in one's element

indicators.note: on means the officer's pieces ride after the horse in an across answer

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: A young lieutenant feels at home on horseback, in his element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is in one's' is a link playing on the idiom 'in one's element'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobalt is a metallic chemical element, number 27.

clue.text: Most orderly, so fails to go into what could be given for tat

indicators.note: to go into means the second word is placed within the first

parts.words: what could be given for tat
parts.note: the phrase tit for tat, meaning retaliation in kind
dies, as an engine fails or stops

explanation.walkthrough: 'What could be given for tat' points to the idiom tit for tat; 'so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidiest is the superlative of tidy, meaning neatest or most orderly.

clue.text: Oil producer's share not worked out

definitions.note: the 's after producer stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay

indicators.note: worked out suggests letters reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: An oil company's share has not been calculated yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worked out' rearranges SHARE and NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The waters between Britain and Norway hold major offshore oilfields.

clue.text: Cavalry regiment in breeches once

indicators.note: in places the regiment's letter inside the old garment

parts.note: hose formerly meant breeches or close-fitting leggings for men
R is an abbreviation for regiment

explanation.surface: A cavalry regiment once wore breeches as uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regiment' is not part of the definition: it supplies R, and HORSE alone means cavalry.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse is a collective term for mounted troops, as in 'a thousand horse'.

clue.text: Made fun of being poorly dressed

explanation.definitionFit: Ragged means teased in British slang and also clothed in rags.

clue.text: Pleased last of haze is clearing

parts.note: glad means pleased

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased that the mist is lifting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' is a link; the stray apostrophe in the held text is an OCR mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A glade is an open clearing in a forest.

clue.text: It may be low on furthest point of horizon

definitions.text: It may be low on furthest point of horizon

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

indicators.note: the furthest point of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A celestial body may sit low on the far horizon.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as wordplay, 'low' is the cow's call and 'on' places it before the last letter of 'horizon'; read whole, it describes a low-hanging satellite.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earth's satellite often appears low on the horizon at rising or setting.

clue.text: Estuary commonly spoken of as dark brown

indicators.note: a common or Cockney speaker drops initial aitches, so the first letter goes

parts.note: the Humber is the estuary in north-east England

explanation.surface: Locals refer to a river mouth as murky brown.
explanation.walkthrough: The Humber is an estuary in north-east England; 'commonly' pronounced it loses its H. 'As' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Umber is a natural earth pigment giving a dark brown colour.

clue.text: Hate to use a sawn-off weapon in spirit of vengeance?

indicators.note: sawn-off means the end is cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: a bomb is a weapon
Ate is the Greek goddess of ruin and reckless vengeance

explanation.surface: Someone loathes the idea of using a sawn-off shotgun to take revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sawn-off' cuts BOMB to BOM, and 'in' is taken literally; Ate appears in Julius Caesar 'with Ate by his side' crying havoc.
explanation.definitionFit: To abominate is to loathe or detest intensely.

clue.text: Union non-member a target for Coleridge's seaman

parts.note: a wedding is the union of a couple

explanation.surface: A non-unionised worker becomes a target for an old sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Rime of the Ancient Mariner, the old seaman stops a guest on his way to a wedding to tell his tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge's Ancient Mariner buttonholes a man going to a marriage feast to hear his story.
